name: Ultimate Cheeseburger Wellington
description: A cheeseburger wrapped in golden puff pastry with cheddar, caramelized onions, pickles and burger sauce.

source.note: The supplied Reel did not provide an accessible written recipe. Measurements are Food Expert-developed.

steps.title: Make the burger sauce
steps.text: Mix mayonnaise, ketchup, yellow mustard, chopped pickles, pickle juice, garlic powder, onion powder and black pepper. Refrigerate.

steps.title: Caramelize the onions
steps.text: Cook thinly sliced onion with oil, butter and salt until deeply golden, soft and jammy. Add small splashes of water if sticking. Add optional sugar if desired. Cool completely.

steps.title: Form the patties
steps.text: Gently mix ground beef with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and Worcestershire sauce. Divide into four approximately 125 g portions and shape into patties.

steps.title: Sear the patties
steps.text: Sear about 2–3 minutes per side for a browned crust. Transfer to a clean plate and cool; the burgers will finish cooking in the oven.

steps.title: Prepare the pastry
steps.text: Keep puff pastry cold. Roll only as needed so each piece can fully enclose one burger without stretching.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Layer patty, cheddar, burger sauce, pickles and caramelized onions. Leave about 2–3 cm of clean pastry around the edge. Brush edge with egg wash, fold, seal firmly and place seam-side down.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Chill the assembled Wellingtons to firm the pastry fat and help maintain shape.

steps.title: Egg wash and vent
steps.text: Brush with beaten egg and water. Sprinkle sesame seeds and optional flaky salt. Cut 2–3 small vents on top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake in a fully preheated oven until deeply golden and crisp. Check the beef center with a thermometer; ground beef should reach at least 71°C.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Rest before cutting. Serve with burger sauce, crispy fries, extra pickles or a fresh salad.

donenessCues: Pastry is deeply golden, crisp and visibly flaky.
Caramelized onions are soft, glossy, deeply golden and jammy.
Cheese is melted and mostly contained within the pastry.
chefNotes: Keep pastry cold; warm filling can melt the pastry fat before baking.
Do not overfill with sauce or wet ingredients.
Cool the patties and onions before assembly.
Resting improves slicing and keeps the filling from rushing out.
commonMistakes: Soggy pastry from warm or wet filling.
Wellington bursting because of overfilling or weak seams.
Dry beef from cooking the patties too long before baking.
Raw pastry from pastry being too thick or an oversized filling.
substitutions: Use locally available frozen puff pastry.
Regular cheddar works well; mature cheddar gives a stronger cheeseburger flavor.
Dill pickles are preferred; sour cucumber pickles can work.
If Worcestershire sauce is unavailable, a small amount of soy sauce can be used, creating a more Asian-leaning flavor.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly. Reheat in an oven or air fryer for better pastry texture; reheat until thoroughly hot.
